description: Canonical cross-platform registry for UI workflows used by clients, staff and administrators across React Web and Flutter Mobile, including frontend routes and public API endpoint references.

workflows.description: Shared home workflow for coastal discovery and account entry. React Web introduces BLUEVERSE's coastal scope and restores signed-in account state. Flutter Mobile restores the saved session at launch and opens Dashboard for an authenticated user; signed-out users see a coastal onboarding carousel with Skip to the final Sign in/Create account choices. Signing out of the final active device account returns to the carousel. Coastal service workflows are not yet available.

Shared sign-in workflow at /signin using protected browser cookies or Flutter secure storage. Up to five browser/device accounts can be selected, and each account signs out from its own active session.
Shared account creation at /signup. Registration does not accept a returnTo destination: successful registration signs the new account in and opens Profile.

Shared authenticated profile workflow. Both clients show server-owned personal details, support profile updates and password changes, allow session review, require password verification to end another device or all sessions, and provide a final-confirmation account deletion flow subject to server system-role policy.
Shared signed-in overview of the current account and an honest preview of BLUEVERSE coastal service areas planned for future availability. Login-session details are managed in Profile.

Authenticated creation page with permission-aware Create a plan/Plan history tabs, reduced-motion-aware directional transitions without an intermediate loading screen, inline catalogue status and a coastal hero, destination-local date and time validation, optional interests, returned suggestions, explicit choice and snapshot-linked draft save/append. Guests return here after sign-in. React and Flutter use the same public API and permissions with responsive web and native layouts.

Public planner introduction for signed-in and signed-out visitors: what planning offers, how it works, optional live inspiration and CTA to the protected creation page. The public introduction has no account sidebar or redundant self-link. The planner is globally reachable from web navigation and mobile account, sign-in, onboarding and planner menus. Personal planning pages use permission-aware Create a plan and Plan history links. Dedicated illustrative planner images support each section.
Permission-aware administration entry for users who hold at least one current administration read grant. React administration hides home-section marketing navigation while retaining account actions.

Read the application-defined permission catalogue and follow its role assignments. Permission codes are managed by the service; role grants can be added or removed by authorized role editors. React administration hides home-section marketing navigation while retaining account actions.

Read roles, create roles, update details and permission assignments, and delete eligible non-system roles. Read and action permissions are checked together on the server. React administration hides home-section marketing navigation while retaining account actions.

Read and manage user accounts, including details, active state, password resets and role assignments. Read and action grants are combined; system-role operations and account deletion rules are enforced on the server. React administration hides home-section marketing navigation while retaining account actions.

Global, branded not-found recovery. React unknown paths stay in the address bar and render inside the shared site shell; Flutter presents the recovery page within its app navigation. Both offer a clear return to the coastal home page.
Global, branded server and rendering-error recovery with retry and home navigation. React renders the recovery content in its shared header/main/footer shell; Flutter uses its app navigation layout.
Revisit a caller-owned search, inspect permitted workflow progress and evidence, and save or append a suggestion through the shared public API.

Caller-owned plan history with Create a plan/Plan history tabs, reduced-motion-aware directional transitions without an intermediate loading screen, inline history-read status and a coastal hero, draft/confirmed/past filters, per-page search, reset, condition-check refinement, 10/20/25/50 page-size selection, and paged plan cards. React and Flutter preserve owner scoping and use the shared public API.

Plan details with a clearer itinerary timeline, draft editing/reorder/remove, confirmation, deletion and condition review/history. Existing shared backend behavior and Flutter workflows are preserved.

Shared React and Flutter marine lookup workflow with matching condition evidence and server-owned suitability outcomes; neither client reclassifies conditions. Both clients preserve signed decimal coordinates; Flutter does not replay ambiguous assessment writes. Both clients show activity data as unavailable with retry while preserving saved records and independent condition lookup; dependent profile draft/edit/review and evaluation actions are disabled until published activity data is available. Deactivation remains independent and typed error adapters retain availability metadata. React provides accessible workflow navigation, a location/time guide and plain-language explanations of unchanged server results. React offers a shared account-menu entry with the Marine read grant. React sidebar and page tabs use the same label: Coastal conditions (shared display-label source). React adds a responsive editorial hero with newly generated ocean swell and shoreline imagery. Imagery is decorative, not observed conditions, stored records or proof of safety. The React hero places its image above its text panel at every screen width. React uses a persistent shared heading and introduction, followed by the existing pill tabs above each stacked hero and content panel. Tabs stick below the site header during scrolling. Switching Marine tabs animates only the panel with reduced-motion support and uses inline initial-read feedback; first entry, explicit retries, writes and Auth retain normal loading feedback. Flutter uses one native Marine shell with the shared labels Coastal conditions, Coastal evidence and Activity safety limits, pinned navigation, stacked local photographic heroes and reduced-motion-aware panel transitions. Dashboard and account-menu entry require the read grant. Native public requests reuse the selected secure account credentials, and changing accounts or grants resets or removes protected content. Tab bootstrap reads remain inline; explicit reads and production writes retain shared loading feedback. Flutter renders sourced wind, wave, swell and rain values with units and explicit unavailable fields. UNKNOWN results survive absent condition evidence. Time input is normalized to UTC; pull-to-refresh reads conditions without creating another assessment.

Shared React and Flutter history of stored marine conditions and suitability assessments, including immutable values, per-factor cited criteria and clear disclosure of incomplete legacy evidence. Coordinate filters preserve signed decimals and malformed nonblank input is rejected before querying. Both clients show activity data as unavailable with retry while preserving saved records and independent condition lookup; dependent profile draft/edit/review and evaluation actions are disabled until published activity data is available. Deactivation remains independent and typed error adapters retain availability metadata. React refresh/filter requests preserve independently successful datasets and distinguish unavailable history from empty results. React sidebar and page tabs use the same label: Coastal evidence (shared display-label source). React adds a responsive editorial hero with newly generated coastal field notebook and compass imagery. Imagery is decorative, not observed conditions, stored records or proof of safety. The React hero places its image above its text panel at every screen width. React uses a persistent shared heading and introduction, followed by the existing pill tabs above each stacked hero and content panel. Tabs stick below the site header during scrolling. Switching Marine tabs animates only the panel with reduced-motion support and uses inline initial-read feedback; first entry, explicit retries, writes and Auth retain normal loading feedback. Flutter uses one native Marine shell with the shared labels Coastal conditions, Coastal evidence and Activity safety limits, pinned navigation, stacked local photographic heroes and reduced-motion-aware panel transitions. Dashboard and account-menu entry require the read grant. Native public requests reuse the selected secure account credentials, and changing accounts or grants resets or removes protected content. Tab bootstrap reads remain inline; explicit reads and production writes retain shared loading feedback. Flutter loads readings and assessments independently, distinguishes failed from empty data, retains labelled last-loaded records after a failed refresh and provides retry.

Shared React and Flutter profile workflow for evidence-backed immutable drafts, per-factor source and rationale, independent review and approval, effective-version history, and permission-matched deactivation. Both clients allow profile inspection with read permission; only mutations require manage. Limits accept at most two decimal places without silent rounding. Both clients show activity data as unavailable with retry while preserving saved records and independent condition lookup; dependent profile draft/edit/review and evaluation actions are disabled until published activity data is available. Deactivation remains independent and typed error adapters retain availability metadata. React groups limits and supporting evidence by factor and offers retry for unavailable saved profiles; browser input validates the shared precision, range and caution contract before submission. React sidebar and page tabs use the same label: Activity safety limits (shared display-label source). React adds a responsive editorial hero with newly generated kayak and safety equipment prepared on shore imagery. Imagery is decorative, not observed conditions, stored records or proof of safety. The React hero places its image above its text panel at every screen width. React uses a persistent shared heading and introduction, followed by the existing pill tabs above each stacked hero and content panel. Tabs stick below the site header during scrolling. Switching Marine tabs animates only the panel with reduced-motion support and uses inline initial-read feedback; first entry, explicit retries, writes and Auth retain normal loading feedback. Flutter uses one native Marine shell with the shared labels Coastal conditions, Coastal evidence and Activity safety limits, pinned navigation, stacked local photographic heroes and reduced-motion-aware panel transitions. Dashboard and account-menu entry require the read grant. Native public requests reuse the selected secure account credentials, and changing accounts or grants resets or removes protected content. Tab bootstrap reads remain inline; explicit reads and production writes retain shared loading feedback. Flutter exposes profile read retry, distinguishes unavailable from empty profiles, labels retained data and shows absent caution values as not configured. Create/version, independent review and confirmed deactivation retain the shared permission and evidence contract.

Public coastal discovery across destinations, activities and offerings. Flutter reads all result pages, retains available data on refresh failures and keeps discovery and map tabs alive. Both clients use public place search and nearby search, opt-in device location, and a real MapLibre map from registered configuration; exploration does not provide turn-by-turn routing. Flutter requests the best available foreground location accuracy with fine/coarse Android permission, respects reduced access, and explicitly removes background location permission.

Destination profile with geographic details and linked offerings. Marine conditions, operations advisories and biodiversity predictions are optional context with explicit unavailable states, provenance and uncertainty. Flutter loads the destination before optional context and isolates each pushed detail route so late responses cannot replace another destination.

Offering details and departure windows with public operational availability evaluation. Flutter loads the offering independently of schedules, evaluates exact active schedule windows or an explicit Asia/Colombo window converted to UTC, and distinguishes unavailable checks from confirmed availability. No booking or cancellation workflow is implied.

Authenticated personal coastal wishlist for destinations, activities and offerings, with filtering and removal. Saves are scoped to the active account and protected against duplicate in-flight actions.

Permission-gated coastal management for Destinations, Activities and Offerings & Schedules with dedicated React subsection routes and retained Flutter tabs. Supports authoring, schedule maintenance and item-specific publication review and transitions. Existing authenticated read-only dependency/context adapters are retained for support; no diagnostics tab or executable Agentic AI is exposed.

Separate searchable Assessment page with draft CRUD, Publish using submit, durable typed delivery, scoped activity, evidence and review. Agent delivery remains disconnected before G07. React list introductions and light photo-over-copy hero cards reuse distinct coastal imagery; sticky pill tab styling is retained, with a reduced-motion-aware 420ms directional slide-and-fade of the React content column. Compact 500ms live search with local loading, read-only detail summaries and explicit Edit draft forms retain shared chrome. Evidence changes are DRAFT-only, including removal. Shared white record cards, header-aligned sticky section tabs with directional transitions, per-page cursor controls and refresh-safe query view intent; Logs-origin details suppress mutations and show correlation references only in Logs. Flutter rebuilds the native workspace, forms, details, records, search and activity with responsive light photo-over-copy heroes, wrapping metadata, pinned navigation and reduced-motion-aware 420ms content transitions; existing permissions and public API workflows remain.

Separate Alert page with draft CRUD, publish/resolve, searchable lifecycle and audience filters, pagination and scoped activity; no agent dispatch. React list introductions and light photo-over-copy hero cards reuse distinct coastal imagery; sticky pill tab styling is retained, with a reduced-motion-aware 420ms directional slide-and-fade of the React content column. Compact 500ms live search with local loading, read-only detail summaries and explicit Edit draft forms retain shared chrome. Shared white record cards, header-aligned sticky section tabs with directional transitions, per-page cursor controls and refresh-safe query view intent; Logs-origin details suppress mutations and show correlation references only in Logs. Flutter rebuilds the native workspace, forms, details, records, search and activity with responsive light photo-over-copy heroes, wrapping metadata, pinned navigation and reduced-motion-aware 420ms content transitions; existing permissions and public API workflows remain.

Audit-granted retained Assessment/Alert records with compact 500ms title search, per-record activity and 5/10/25/50/100-record cursor paging. Owner/reviewer/manager scopes remain server-enforced. Header-aligned sticky category tabs animate directionally and persist kind=assessments|alerts across refresh. Opened record details are read-only, hide lifecycle/evidence mutations, and provide styled correlation references without actor UUIDs. React uses a list introduction and light photo-over-copy hero with category-specific labels, retaining the existing image and sticky pill tabs. React Logs switches animate the introduction, hero and records together with a reduced-motion-aware 420ms directional slide-and-fade. Flutter rebuilds the native workspace, forms, details, records, search and activity with responsive light photo-over-copy heroes, wrapping metadata, pinned navigation and reduced-motion-aware 420ms content transitions; existing permissions and public API workflows remain.

endpoints.description: Owner-only unpublished draft evidence removal with current version, retained audit tombstone and deferred private-byte cleanup.
Audit/read-gated retained assessments including own drafts and cancellations; scoped title filters and cursor pagination.
Audit/read-gated retained alerts including inactive and withdrawn records within manager or owner scope.
